svg.text: Algorithm 4 — Incremental row algorithm (lazy reduction, rows bottom-up)

text.tspan: Same matrix: R ← D, V ← I. Rows are now processed from the bottom up. For row i, lft(i) is the earliest column whose
lowest non-zero entry lies in row i (green column); it is applied to the orange columns, eliminating the ringed entries.
Row 8: columns with lowest entry here: 3, 8. lft(8) = 3 (green) is the pivot, (8, 3).
Apply it to column 8 (orange): the later column whose lowest entry is also row 8.
Column 8 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 8 = {1, 4, 5, 6}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 7: columns with lowest entry here: 6, 7. lft(7) = 6 (green) is the pivot, (7, 6).
Apply it to column 7 (orange): the later column whose lowest entry is also row 7.
Column 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 7 = {1, 5}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 6: columns with lowest entry here: 8. lft(6) = 8 (green) is the pivot, (6, 8).
No later column has its lowest entry in row 6: nothing to apply.
Row 5: columns with lowest entry here: 1, 7. lft(5) = 1 (green) is the pivot, (5, 1).
Apply it to column 7 (orange): the later column whose lowest entry is also row 5. Columns 3, 6, 8 (gray) are left alone: pivot below.
Column 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 7 = {2, 4}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 4: columns with lowest entry here: 4, 5, 7. lft(4) = 4 (green) is the pivot, (4, 4).
Apply it to columns 5, 7 (orange): the later columns whose lowest entry is also row 4. Column 8 (gray) is left alone: pivot below.
Columns 5, 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 5 = {1, 2, 3} column 7 = {3}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 3: columns with lowest entry here: 5, 7. lft(3) = 5 (green) is the pivot, (3, 5).
Apply it to column 7 (orange): the later column whose lowest entry is also row 3.
Column 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 7 = {1, 2}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 2: columns with lowest entry here: 2, 7. lft(2) = 2 (green) is the pivot, (2, 2).
Apply it to column 7 (orange): the later column whose lowest entry is also row 2. Columns 4, 5, 6 (gray) are left alone: pivot below.
Column 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 7 = 0.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 1: no column has its lowest non-zero entry in this row (columns 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 have entries here, but their pivots lie further down).
lft(1) is undefined: row 1 holds no pivot.
Identical to the lazy (column) reduction of Algorithm 1 (Lemma 5.1), obtained row by row instead of column by column.

svg.text: j ← lft(i) ▷ earliest column with low(j) = i
for j′ > j with low(j′) = i: ▷ only columns whose lowest entry is row i
▷ columns with a pivot further down are left alone:
▷ same decomposition as the lazy reduction (Lemma 5.1)
